blocks.text: By the end of this chapter, students will be able to:

items: Understand and explain network architecture, its fundamental concepts and become proficient in network diagnostic tools and commands.
Set up and configure home networks effectively and develop network troubleshooting skills and differentiate between network connection types.
Understand and measure network bandwidth and latency, and appreciate the importance of network load balancing, network security, data backup and recovery.

blocks.text: This chapter introduces the fundamental concepts of computer networks and explains how devices communicate with each other. Students learn about network architecture, key components, and the basic working of networks. It covers network models and layers, particularly the OSI model, along with different network topologies and types. The chapter also explains common networking devices such as NICs, switches, routers, modems, and wireless access points.

Students are introduced to essential protocols and services like TCP/IP, HTTP, FTP, and DNS, as well as concepts of IP addressing, IPv4/IPv6, subnetting, and NAT. They learn how to set up and configure home networks, including wired and wireless connections, and understand Wi-Fi security and encryption. The use of network diagnostic tools such as ping and ipconfig is also discussed. Finally, the chapter highlights network performance, security measures, and real-world practices to ensure safe and efficient communication.
